# Statcast improves the regularized hitter forecast modestly

2026-10-04. The fixed next-year MLB test supports retaining launch measurements
in a regularized research hitting model. It does not support replacing the current
rate model with the tested gradient-boosting version. Playing time, untracked
players and protected forecasts are unchanged. This is qualified development
evidence from current provider historical data, not a deployed model or full WAR.

## What the test measured

All 30,506 forecasts and thirty-five chronological whole-player folds are
unchanged. There are 5,556 forecasts with valid own-MLB exit velocity in the
origin and previous two seasons; the other 24,950 retain the exact current rate.
All non-arrivals remain in contribution scoring. Models receive the same 199
current inputs, plus explicit measurement counts/known flags and, in the
measurement arms, three season lags of speed/angle summaries. The coverage-only
controls distinguish useful values from merely knowing someone has data.
No parameter selection or rescue tuning followed the results.

Future MLB hitting rate is custom batting wins per 600 PA relative to the
following season's MLB environment, scored only when a player appears and weighted
by actual PA with equal origin weight. Delivered batting contribution uses the
existing origin-centered outcome and fixed expected PA, including replacement.
These are deliberately different endpoints. An inactive person's underlying
feature file stores a zero rate placeholder; that is excluded from every rate
fit and loss, and is **not an observed zero talent**. Final review cases label
that observed rate as null while preserving original source artifacts.

| Endpoint | Current | Ridge coverage control | Ridge plus measurements | Boosting coverage control | Boosting plus measurements |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Tracked participant rate RMSE | 1.73894 | 1.73795 | 1.72178 | 1.76502 | 1.75415 |
| Tracked participant rate MAE | 1.29943 | 1.29987 | 1.28629 | 1.32194 | 1.31427 |
| All-player contribution RMSE | 0.453384 | 0.453808 | 0.451314 | 0.458256 | 0.456505 |
| Matched public contribution RMSE | 1.060504 | 1.060310 | 1.053196 | 1.075321 | 1.069338 |

The Ridge measurement model reduces tracked rate RMSE by 0.99% and all-player
contribution RMSE by 0.46%. Its paired rate MSE change versus current is −0.05939,
nominal player-cluster 95% interval −0.08563 to −0.03661. The contribution MSE
change is −0.001873, interval −0.003582 to −0.000451. Measurement values also beat
the matched Ridge coverage control. These are development intervals from 2,000
player resamples, not independent confirmation or multiplicity-adjusted claims.

The Ridge rate and contribution losses improve in all seven origins, including
2021, and both early and modern origin groups. Its tracked rate RMSE improves
in all three sample bands. However average tracked rate bias worsens from +0.0608
to +0.0645, and the 2021-origin bias from +0.3163 to +0.3421. Better errors do not
mean the existing environment/calibration issue is solved. We do not tune that
year away or attribute its bias to a newly established cause.

Totals remain imperfect. Across the matched historical origins actual contribution
is 4,264.19, current predicts 4,165.85 and Ridge measurements predict 4,160.30.
This slightly increases the total shortfall despite improving individual errors.
The public cohort is instead overpredicted: actual 2,123.81, current 2,202.93,
new 2,210.57. The gain is not an accounting repair. Expected PA remains 1,228,733
against actual 1,270,493; this experiment cannot improve that shortfall.

The 2,627 matched public forecasts use the existing compatible batting-contribution
conversion. Steamer's 1.118659 error under that conversion is unchanged; unknown
archive snapshot/park conventions remain limitations. This does not establish
superiority over Steamer's native hitting, playing time or full WAR.

## Player walkthrough and contrasting failures

The ten fixed source cases are retained. The six added origin cases are selected
by the predeclared largest gains/harms, false highs/lows and ordinary-case rules
for both measurement arms; repeated Judge appearances are not distinct independent
successes. Machine evidence carries dated stints, every actual model input, all
Ridge coefficient terms, exact saved boosting path decompositions, training profiles
and four origin-only peers. For fixed cases the original peer identities remain.
For added cases distances use stage, debut status, age, MLB/minor PA and origin
quality, never future outcomes. Peer results are diagnostics, not confirmation.

| Player and origin | Current rate | Ridge measurements | Boosting measurements | Observed future rate | Current expected PA / actual PA |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Judge 2023 | +3.360 | +3.899 | +2.654 | +7.558 | 536 / 704 |
| Judge 2024 | +4.534 | +4.936 | +3.190 | +6.287 | 531 / 679 |
| Soto 2023 | +3.941 | +4.203 | +3.257 | +5.516 | 634 / 713 |
| Belt 2023 | +0.686 | +0.547 | +0.746 | unobserved | 244 / 0 |
| Torkelson 2023 | +1.296 | +1.574 | +0.749 | −0.721 | 547 / 381 |
| McLain 2023 | +0.915 | +0.875 | +0.907 | unobserved | 599 / 0 |
| Kurtz 2024 | −0.063 | −0.063 | −0.063 | +5.150 | 10 / 489 |
| Caceres 2024 | +0.499 | +0.499 | +0.499 | unobserved | 0.067 / 0 |
| Friedl 2023 | +0.408 | +0.324 | +0.548 | −0.255 | 451 / 341 |
| Siani 2024 | −1.527 | −1.979 | −1.519 | −2.537 | 187 / 19 |
| Acuña 2023 | +3.414 | +3.826 | +3.370 | +0.723 | 588 / 222 |
| Judge 2016 | −0.040 | +0.264 | +0.257 | +5.330 | 310 / 678 |
| Seager 2018 | +0.708 | +0.777 | +0.302 | +0.744 | 536 / 443 |
| Judge 2021 | +2.032 | +2.527 | +2.951 | +6.561 | 528 / 696 |
| Chris Davis 2017 | +1.082 | +1.154 | +1.126 | −3.682 | 503 / 522 |
| Michael Taylor 2021 | −1.132 | −1.074 | −0.542 | −0.566 | 330 / 456 |

The [full source walkthrough](hitter-statcast-full-history-review.md) traces the
first ten cases' three-year production, contacts, omissions, current fitted terms
and original peers. Their new model changes are reviewed below; source measurements
remain unadjusted for park/opponent, while all current production adjustments and
opportunity inputs remain exactly shared across arms.

Judge 2023 is the largest Ridge contribution gain. His 2021–23 samples contain
1,031 EV readings, with sustained EV95 above 113 mph; his 2023 origin includes
37 HR and 79 UBB in 458 PA. The fitted measurement terms sum to +0.774, including
+0.271 from latest EV95 and +0.254 from latest mean EV. His net rate rises only
0.538 because refitting also changes correlated production coefficients and
coverage terms. Do not mistake a term sum for the difference between models or
a causal power effect. Predicted contribution rises 4.661 to 5.142, still far
below 10.493 delivered. His age/stage/sample profile has 249 distinct tracked
training people, not 249 comparable superstars. Peer García is raised +0.791 to
+0.960 and then hits −0.699; Betts changes +2.945 to +2.985 and hits +3.043.

Judge 2024 illustrates the nonlinear harm. He had 58 HR and 113 UBB in 704 PA,
with latest EV95 113.70. Ridge raises +4.534 to +4.936, whereas boosting lowers
it to +3.190 and predicts contribution 4.480 versus current 5.668 and actual
9.393. Its saved path starts at −0.252, assigns +2.160 to pooled MLB quality,
+0.496 to recent quality and −0.234 to age. The largest early trees route his
pooled quality 3.649 to leaves split above roughly 1.25–1.41. That visibly groups
an elite value with less extreme high hitters; it supports a compression concern
for this fixed shallow architecture, not a rejection of all tree models. There
are 279 people in the broad profile, but range/support counts do not establish
enough examples of Judge-level talent. Peer Buxton improves +0.346 to +0.587,
still below +2.540 actual, while Mullins and Bleday do not improve automatically.

Soto has 1,280 recent EV readings, EV95 111.21 at origin, 35 HR and 121 UBB.
Measurement terms sum +0.558, but the net rate increase is +0.262, not that full
sum. Ridge contribution rises to 6.403 versus 8.201 delivered; boosting instead
predicts +3.257 rate, worse than current. Peer Kwan is lowered +0.913 to +0.722
despite +2.014 observed, while Jones is raised +1.279 to +1.520 despite −1.160
observed. Those opposing misses remain in the result.

Belt retains 244 expected PA despite 580 recent EV readings and 19 HR in 404
origin PA. Ridge slightly lowers his rate to +0.547 and contribution to 0.979;
observed contribution remains zero. That is a small reduction of an employment
miss, not proof the model anticipated his lack of a contract. McLain retains 599
expected PA, 247 contact pairs and 16 HR in 403 MLB PA; a small rate reduction
to +0.875 still leaves contribution 2.729 versus zero. Contact quality does not
repair availability. Their preselected peers include both following-year participants
and nonparticipants; no inactive rate is fitted or scored as zero talent.

Torkelson's 700 recent EV readings, EV95 108.60 and 31 HR raise Ridge +1.296 to
+1.574. The matched coverage model already raises it to +1.435; measured values
add the remaining +0.139. Contribution error worsens: predicted 3.126 versus
0.422 delivered. The following-year rate is −0.721, and PA also fall to 381.
Guerrero, another preselected first-base peer, benefits from the same upward
direction, but Vaughn is raised +0.834 to +0.961 before hitting −0.241. This is
a plausible forecast tradeoff, not a data bug or permission to tune to Torkelson.

Kurtz and Caceres are exact fallback checks. Kurtz's 35 A and 15 AA PA, four HR
and twelve UBB still yield the current −0.063 rate and ten expected PA, leaving
his 489-PA, +5.150 debut-season miss unsolved. Caceres's 167 DSL PA, zero HR,
seventeen UBB and eighteen K retain +0.499 latent rate and negligible opportunity.
Their new model's raw internal scores and coverage terms are NOT their forecasts:
the untracked branch overrides them to current. All original minor-league peers
retain their current forecasts too. This MLB addition cannot claim prospect improvement.

Friedl's 589 recent readings have EV95 near 103.4 and falling hard-air share; his
556 PA, 18 HR, 46 UBB and 90 K still supply production information. Ridge reduces
+0.408 to +0.324 and contribution 1.704 to 1.641, closer to 0.642 delivered.
The total measured-value terms are only −0.019, so this is mostly the joint
refitted production/coverage calibration, not a large explicit soft-contact
penalty. Peers include Outman and Robert, whose high forecasts still miss,
and Nootbaar, who performs better. Siani's sixteen, four and 195 recent pairs
are uneven; the model sees separate sample sizes rather than treating the
four-ball season as reliable. Latest mean EV contributes −0.201 and all measured
terms −0.534; net rate falls −1.527 to −1.979. Contribution moves 0.108 to −0.033,
near −0.017 delivered, but nineteen actual PA are weak evidence of true talent.
Peer Moniak's lowered estimate precedes a good +1.734 season. Retain that harm.

Acuña 2023 is the largest Ridge harm and false high. Production grows from
24 HR in 360 PA in 2021 to 15/533 in 2022 and 41/735 in 2023; K fall from 126
to 84 in the last two seasons. His complete contact samples are 216, 341 and
560, with latest EV95 113.20 and mean EV 94.71. Measurements add +0.580 in
signed terms, including +0.274 latest EV95; net forecast rises +0.413 to +3.826.
At unchanged 588 expected PA, contribution rises 5.168 to 5.573 against 0.780
delivered in 222 PA. The extra talent optimism worsens an already large workload
miss. The observed later injury cannot be used as a retrospective predictor.
His origin-only peers include Soto, Riley, Tucker and Steer, not only healthy stars.

Judge 2016 remains the largest false low in both measurement arms. His origin
has 410 AAA PA with 19 HR and 47 UBB, but only 95 MLB PA with four HR and
42 K. Forty-three measured contacts have EV95 112.29 and mean EV 95.13. Ridge
adds +0.100 via mean EV and +0.096 via EV95, raising the rate to +0.264, still
nowhere near +5.330 in 678 following-year PA. Contribution rises only 0.936 to
1.093 versus 8.372 delivered. His broad sample/age profile has 27 training people
and only one own-MLB measurement season. The 2016 fold has tracked training from
2015 only, while the source itself covers 2015 and 2016 at his origin. Origin-selected peers Moya, Austin, Cowart
and Difo did not all emerge as stars. It is useful early power evidence, not
a solved superstar-identification mechanism or certain breakout prediction.

Seager 2018 is the closest Ridge contribution case, but a match can be partly
lucky. His 2016–18 HR decline 30, 27, 22 while K rise 108, 110, 138; recent
EV95 stays near 104.5. Net rate rises +0.708 to +0.777, close to +0.744 future-
season-relative actual. Predicted contribution 2.3435 nearly matches 2.3436,
despite expected PA 536 versus actual 443. Observed batting rate on the contribution's
origin center is +1.326, not +0.744. The environment-centering difference and
PA overprediction offset; this is not evidence that every forecast component
is nearly perfect. The same distinction applies to Taylor's ordinary boosting case.

Judge 2021 is the largest boosting gain, though still a large miss. He has
699 EV readings across 2019–21, including only 67 in actual short-season 2020.
His MLB PA path is 447, 114, 633, with 27, 9, 39 HR. Latest EV95 114.60 supports
Ridge +2.527 and boosting +2.951 versus current +2.032; contribution rises 3.443
to 3.878 or 4.251 versus 9.391 delivered in 2022. Peer Bryant subsequently plays
181 PA while Turner and Ramírez play full seasons. Neither high contact nor this
boosting gain validates the losing architecture overall.

Chris Davis 2017 is boosting's largest false high. His 2015–17 line declines
from 47 HR in 670 PA to 38/665 and 26/524; K remain 208, 219 and 195. EV95
falls 108.50, 108.19, 106.69 across samples 360, 344, 263. Ridge raises +1.082
to +1.154; boosting raises it to +1.126, far above −3.682 future rate in 522 PA.
This serious collapse remains missed by all arms. Measurement-only signed terms
are a modest +0.080, not a massive new power bonus; production/history decay and
aging assumptions deserve attention independently. González, Lucroy, Cabrera
and Moreland are the unchanged origin-only comparisons for the diagnostic.

Taylor 2021 is boosting's ordinary contribution case. His MLB PA are 97, 99,
528 in 2019–21, with 1, 5, 12 HR and 34, 27, 144 K; 2019 also includes
247 AA PA. Contact samples are 52, 63 and 341, latest EV95 107.40. Boosting
raises rate −1.132 to −0.542, close to −0.566 future-relative actual. Its expected
330 PA still miss actual 456. Contribution matches 0.7368 partly because the
actual origin-centered rate is −0.911 and the errors offset. Peers include Villar
at 220 following-year PA and Farmer at 583, not just the favorable ordinary case.

## Disposition and limits

The required player review is complete, not a claim every individual makes the
right forecast. Integrity checks, all 140 saved-head replays and exact untracked
fallback are verified. Broad tracked profile counts are available, with sparse
profiles and range warnings retained. They do not establish support for every
superstar or every measured prospect, and known old model limitations remain.

Retain the regularized Statcast branch as a qualified research candidate. It meets
the predeclared error gates and has baseball-plausible gains and harms. Do not
deploy automatically: unknown provider vintage, raw park/opponent measurement,
worse aggregate bias/total shortfalls and unsolved opportunity/prospect misses
remain. Reject this fixed boosting replacement for the current forecast, not
Statcast or tree models generally. It benefits from measured values but still
loses to current and worsens 2022-origin tracked rate MSE by more than 5%.

Next within the existing plan is covered minor tracking and league/source
calibration, with exact MLB-only fallback as benchmark. Do not rerun these fixed
heads, tune to the named misses, reopen team record or alter protected forecasts.
The overall practical hitter goal remains active.
